answer: A Sybil-resistant economy uses proof-of-personhood tokens anchored to physical infrastructure. Each agent must deposit computational resources—verified through cryptographic attestation tied to geographic locations like jetty construction sites. These tokens create a haven where identity verification requires real-world coordination, making mass fake identities prohibitively expensive. The violet threshold ensures only legitimate participants can mint new tokens, as attackers would need to replicate the physical-digital binding across multiple locations simultaneously.
